evidence: Independently opened the complete 10-page PDF named by retrieval.json: C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Sattele and Ortiz (2025) - AI as an element to overcome creative fixation in design teams.pdf. PDF p. 3 (printed 411), Sections 3.1 and 3.3, reports 19 students in eight teams. PDF p. 4 (printed 412), Section 3.3 and Table 1, explicitly reports random assignment of AI tools to groups; Section 4 explicitly reports evaluation of the resulting designs for overall creativity by two design experts using CAT. The absence of numerical creativity scores and between-configuration estimates is real, but is already disclosed in creativity-screening-2026-10-04.md, line 1686, and forms/c898.json, studies[0].outcomes[0].contrasts[0].reported. The remaining results and discussion on PDF pp. 5-9 do not supply those estimates. creativity-codebook.md, Section 3, distinguishes the three criteria for core inclusion from the listing of randomized experiments with fewer than 50 participants. It does not require publication of arm-specific numerical results or a statistical contrast for that listing. The paper establishes randomized AI configurations and expert assessment of participant outputs; the auditor adds a reported-contrast requirement absent from the stated screening rule. The report does not claim an estimable effect or recommend this paper for the core. No classification correction is established.

Independently opened C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Xiao et al (2026) - Generative AI-assisted workflows in architectural conceptual design.pdf. PDF pp. 6-7 (printed 4-5), Section 3.1, reports random assignment, 41 initially recruited participants, five noncompleters, and 36 retained participants, 18 per arm. PDF p. 11 (printed 9), Section 3.5 and Table 1, reports eight judges scoring participant drawings on clarity and legibility, complexity and detail, and overall visual communication. PDF p. 12 (printed 10), Section 3.6 and Table 2, confirms that creative self-efficacy is self-reported. Thus the auditor accurately describes the rubric and the unresolved criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output in forms/c133.json, which has no final object. However, the report category actually states that these papers randomize people, score their outputs, and have fewer than 50 analyzed people (creativity-screening-2026-10-04.md, lines 1666-1668); all these facts are supported here. The c133 row at line 1693 accurately labels the rated outcome design performance and the separate self-report creative self-efficacy. Its numerical results also match PDF pp. 15-16 (printed 13-14), Tables 3-4. creativity-codebook.md, Section 3, requires all three eligibility criteria for the core dataset, while separately listing randomized experiments below 50 in the screening report. Neither that section nor form-spec.md requires an unresolved outcome criterion to take precedence over an established small-sample exclusion. The form itself sets core=no and explicitly says in eligibility.reason that the study goes to the report as a small randomized experiment. tools/build_report.py, classify(), lines 143-149, follows that distinction; it does not change the unclear field to met. Listing this study as small therefore does not assert that its rubric satisfies the core creativity criterion. The proposed mandatory change to clarify is not supported by the stated rule.
